text:
Maya S: quick summary — ran the 'staggered prefetch' experiment across na/eu/apac last night. observed: NA hit-rate ~0.82, EU ~0.68, APAC ~0.39 and tail latency bump in APAC under p95 when region gets cold.

Liam R: thanks — I pulled profiler traces. APAC nodes are frequently falling back to a slower kernel path during KV lookups when batch_queue length < 3. suspect batching heuristics + kernel selector interplay.

Maya S: exact numbers?

Liam R: paste from profiler (trimmed):
```
APAC: avg_batch_size=1.9, kernel=attention_v2_slow_path, KV_CACHE_HIT_RATE=0.41, p95=147ms
NA: avg_batch_size=3.8, kernel=attention_v2_fast_path, KV_CACHE_HIT_RATE=0.81, p95=42ms
EU: avg_batch_size=2.7, kernel=attention_v2_mixed, KV_CACHE_HIT_RATE=0.70, p95=68ms
```

Maya S: that aligns with the hit-rate gaps. when the cache is cold we get small batches and the kernel selector chooses the conservative path -> higher per-token latency.

Rachel G: routing policy question — are requests being routed to APAC cold nodes by policy or is capacity constraints causing fanout?

Liam R: routing is sticky by geo but we had a failover event around 03:12 UTC that pushed some sustained traffic into apac-b. ops-bot shows a brief autoscale then a capacity cap.

ops-bot: deploy @ 03:10 UTC — scale up apac-b pool + apply prefetch window=60s for experiment.

Jin P: I ran a small micro-experiment: bump prefetch window from 10s -> 60s on a subset of APAC replicas. KV cache hit-rate jumped to ~0.68 and avg_batch_size increased to ~3.1. p95 dropped from 147ms -> 72ms.

Maya S: great. can you drop the exact conf we used?

Jin P: config snippet for the canary: 
```
{
  "prefetch": {
    "enabled": true,
    "window_seconds": 60,
    "stagger_strategy": "region_offset",
    "max_prefetch_per_sec": 120
  },
  "batching": {
    "min_batch_threshold": 3,
    "max_delay_ms": 12
  },
  "kernel_selector": {
    "force_warm_path_threshold": 3
  }
}
```

Liam R: interesting note — forcing "force_warm_path_threshold" made the selector pick the fast kernel when batch >=3. that + larger prefetch window moved APAC jumpers into warm cache more often.

Rachel G: any regressions elsewhere? EU had a small increase in memory pressure when prefetch window increased, +2% mem for the pool. NA unaffected.

Maya S: tradeoff seems clear: larger prefetch reduces cold misses but costs memory. we need SLO-friendly defaults per-region.

Liam R: propose: region-tiered defaults — APAC default prefetch 60s, EU 30s, NA 15s. also tweak batcher to allow opportunistic coalesce up to 6ms extra delay when load < target to boost batch size.

Jin P: put a guard: if memory usage > 85% on a replica, reduce prefetch window by 50% for that replica. keeps regressions bounded.

Maya S: can someone run a 6hr canary on apac with those settings and collect per-replica: KV_CACHE_HIT_RATE, avg_batch_size, kernel_path_pct, p50/p95, mem%?

Liam R: I'll schedule it and hook the trace aggregator. Can we add a simple dashboard panel for kernel_path_pct (fast vs slow) by region?

Rachel G: I'll add panels and an alert: if apac p95 > 120ms for > 5m, auto-scale + raise prefetch window.

ops-bot: scheduled: canary apac-prefetch-v2 starting 04:20 UTC for 6h.

Maya S: last thought — we should also consider a short-lived proactive warmup on new node attach: run synthetic priming traffic for top 200 prefixes (from hot-set) for 10s to pre-populate KV. much cheaper than large persistent prefetch.

Jin P: agree — I'll prototype synthetic primer that runs at attach-time and respects rate limits.

Liam R: perfect. once canary completes we'll reconvene with perf graphs. thanks all :thumbsup:
